cards.heading: Why automate
cards.body: Configuring devices one by one by hand is slow and error-prone, and configurations drift apart over time. Automation applies tested changes consistently and quickly to many devices, checks compliance, and frees engineers from repetitive work. The cost: you need skills in programming, APIs and tools.

cards.heading: Three planes
cards.body: The data plane forwards traffic (switching frames, routing packets, applying ACLs). The control plane builds the information needed to forward: routing protocols, STP, ARP. The management plane is how people and tools manage the device: SSH, SNMP, APIs.

cards.heading: Traditional networks
cards.body: Every device runs its own control plane and is configured individually, box by box, usually through the CLI. Network-wide changes mean touching every device.

cards.heading: Controller-based networks
cards.body: An SDN controller centralises (some of) the control plane and the network's configuration. Devices keep the data plane. Administrators and applications work with the controller instead of individual boxes.
cards.example:
Apps / scripts
             │  northbound API (REST)
        [ SDN controller ]
             │  southbound API (NETCONF, RESTCONF, OpenFlow, CLI)
   [switch]  [switch]  [router]

cards.heading: Northbound and southbound
cards.body: The northbound interface (NBI) faces up, to applications and engineers, usually a REST API returning JSON. The southbound interface (SBI) faces down, to the devices: NETCONF, RESTCONF, OpenFlow, OpFlex, or plain SSH/CLI.

cards.heading: Software-Defined Access
cards.body: Cisco SD-Access is a controller-based campus run from Catalyst Center (formerly DNA Center). The underlay is the physical network of routed links (IS-IS). The overlay is built on top: VXLAN tunnels carry traffic, LISP acts as the control plane, and Cisco TrustSec group tags apply policy. Together they form the fabric.

cards.heading: Catalyst Center and traditional management
cards.body: Catalyst Center adds intent-based management: you describe the desired policy and it configures the devices. It also offers assurance (health scores, path traces, issue detection), software image management and a REST API for automation, compared with traditional device-by-device CLI management.
